# Count the topology generated by a small basis

*Medium · [Topology problems](index.md)*

On $X=\{1,2,3\}$, the family $\mathcal B=\{\{1,2\},\{2\},\{2,3\}\}$ is a basis. How many open sets does it generate, including the empty set?

```answer
{"answer":{"kind":"integer","expected":5,"checker_scope":"Exact finite set, interval or count requested in the stated topology only; personal reasoning is not automatically graded."}}
```

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Open sets are all unions of basis members.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Different subfamilies can produce the same union, so count distinct sets.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Worked solution</summary>

Enumerate distinct unions rather than the subfamilies producing them.

1. The empty union gives $\varnothing$, and the three single-member unions give $\{1,2\}$, $\{2\}$ and $\{2,3\}$.
2. Combining the first and third basis members gives $X$. Every other union is already one of these sets.
3. The generated topology has exactly $5$ open sets.

</details>
